clue.text: A name I call myself? Not quite — and wrong gender

definitions.text: A name I call myself? Not quite — and wrong gender

indicators.note: not quite says the name falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the setter's own pseudonym is Brendan, the name he calls himself, echoing the line for Me in the song

explanation.surface: The setter muses that a name for himself is almost right but belongs to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the last letter of the setter's name leaves a woman's name, hence 'wrong gender'; Brenda is also the satirical magazine Private Eye's nickname for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a female name, so the setter's own name trimmed becomes a name suited to the opposite sex.

clue.text: With low level of concentration, so not well done

definitions.meaning: thin or sparse, as rarefied air has little density
of meat, cooked only lightly so it stays red inside

explanation.definitionFit: Rare means both thinly dispersed, like rarefied gas, and lightly cooked, as a steak ordered underdone.

clue.text: Pharisee at home raised fish and birds

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the short word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: at home means in
the cod is a common fish
emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: A religious figure, home again, lifts up fish and fowl.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'raised' means written bottom to top, so the word for at home is turned round before the fish and birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicodemus is the Pharisee in John's Gospel who came to Jesus by night, so the name instances the sect.

clue.text: Religious leader wedding Jack and Elizabeth

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
Bess is a familiar short form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A cleric officiating at the marriage of Jack and Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wedding' is a link that joins the two pieces, as marriage joins the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess heads a community of nuns, so she is a leader within a religious order.

clue.text: Violent commotions from English politician in international events

indicators.note: in places the English politician within the word for the international events

parts.note: test matches are international cricket or rugby fixtures, called tests
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Uproar caused by an English MP at world sporting fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: Test matches are international cricket or rugby games between national sides, usually just called tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempests are violent storms, and by extension any furious uproar or commotion.

clue.text: Movie, the scale of which is apparent in other clues

definitions.text: Movie, the scale of which is apparent in other clues

parts.words: Movie, the scale of which is apparent in other clues
parts.note: a film whose song teaches the musical scale doh, ray, me and so on, each line of which lyric is quoted in another clue of this puzzle

explanation.walkthrough: The other clues quote the film's song lines: a drop of golden sun, a name I call myself, a long long way to run, a needle pulling thread, a note to follow so, a drink with jam and bread, a female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1965 musical film features the song Do-Re-Mi, which walks through each note of the sol-fa scale.

clue.text: Revolutionary taking over horse — a long, long way to run

definitions.text: a long, long way to run

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
on can mean over, as a lid sits on or over a jar

explanation.surface: A revolutionary seizing a horse to cover a great distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link. The definition is the song line for Far.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a footrace of about 26 miles, so it is a very long distance to run.

clue.text: Note to follow so, for work

indicators.note: to follow says the note comes after the word for so

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, meaning so

explanation.surface: A musical note that comes after so, as in the scale.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface quotes the song line for La, 'a note to follow so', but 'Note' here gives just N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergon is a unit of work in physics and also Greek for a deed or task, so it means work.

clue.text: Thomas is example of one that needs no tender attachment

definitions.text: Thomas is example of one that needs no tender attachment

parts.words: Thomas is example of one that needs no tender attachment
parts.note: Thomas of the children's railway stories is a locomotive carrying its water in side tanks, so no tender wagon is coupled behind; tender also hints at affection

explanation.walkthrough: A tender is the wagon behind a steam locomotive holding coal and water; this type carries its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas from the Rev. Awdry's Railway Series is the most famous small steam locomotive that carries water in side tanks instead of a tender.

clue.text: Where snooker players compete for title, dramatically

definitions.meaning: the Sheffield theatre that hosts the World Snooker Championship
the name of Arthur Miller's play about the Salem witch trials

explanation.definitionFit: The Crucible Theatre in Sheffield hosts the world snooker finals, and The Crucible is Arthur Miller's stage play.

clue.text: A party in suits, often, in Canadian city

definitions.meaning: in British court cases the Crown is named as ..., as in ... v. Smith, so it is often a party to proceedings

explanation.walkthrough: Regina, Latin for queen, names the Crown in British prosecutions; the setter calls these suits, a word that also fits queens in suits of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is the capital of the Canadian prairie province of Saskatchewan, and the Latin title of the reigning queen in court case names.

clue.text: Stops selling record, not in use after remix

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: remix, as with a recording, says the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop drops a record that has fallen out of use after a remix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link here; the record comes first and 'remix' shuffles the three words that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: When a firm discontinues a product it ceases to make or sell it, so it stops selling it.

clue.text: A privateer at sea, righting wrongs

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A privately licensed sea raider out on the ocean, putting injustices right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like the privateer's location but signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparative action makes amends, repairing harm done, so it is concerned with putting injustice right.

clue.text: For summer, a drop of golden sun?

definitions.meaning: in building a summer is a large horizontal ... supporting floor joists
a ray of sunlight, as in the song line for Ray

explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season, nor someone who adds up: it is a builder's term for a main supporting timber. 'For' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam is both a long structural timber and a shaft of light such as sunshine.

clue.text: Sadly, inn's gone for modern way to announce its presence

definitions.text: modern way to announce its presence

indicators.note: sadly, as in badly or wretchedly, says the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Regretfully the old pub has closed, replaced by a modern way of advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in inn's is ignored: rearrange INNSGONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing gas-tube advertisement outside a pub or shop announces the premises to passers-by.

clue.text: Inform about one of the little people using a needle pulling thread

indicators.note: about says the word for inform goes round the small person

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: Telling tales about an elf while doing needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little people' suggests fairies or elves, but here means a small person, a titch. The definition is the song line for Sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching is sewing, the act of passing a threaded needle through cloth.

clue.text: Extremely tough way Irish writer leads or Hemingway follows

indicators.note: leads puts the Irish writer at the front, ahead of the way

parts.note: Laurence Sterne, author of Tristram Shandy, was born in Ireland
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A tough route where one novelist goes first, or Hemingway trails.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers two routes to one answer: Sterne followed by ST, or ST followed by Ernest, Hemingway's first name; 'or Hemingway follows' gives the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternest is the superlative of stern, meaning harsh or tough to the highest degree.

clue.text: Wretched state of learner observed in strained voice

indicators.note: wretched means in a bad way, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A pupil's unhappy condition is seen in a strained singing voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observed in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificially high register a male singer forces above his natural range.

clue.text: Island going back and forth in paranoia, irrationally

indicators.note: going back says the letters are read from right to left
in says the answer lies within the word that follows

explanation.surface: An island in the grip of irrational fear, swinging to and fro.
explanation.walkthrough: The island also reads forwards, inside 'irrationally', which is the 'and forth' part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland, famous for its abbey.

clue.text: Incite prison in revolt

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
up means in rebellion, as when people are up in arms

explanation.surface: Inmates rise in a jail riot.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up people is to provoke or rouse them to action, so it is to incite.

clue.text: Kind of film that gets romantic chap excited

indicators.note: excited means agitated, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A film that thrills an amorous man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Panchromatic film is photographic film sensitive to all visible colours of light.

clue.text: After competition each year, a drink with jam and bread

definitions.text: a drink with jam and bread

indicators.note: after says the yearly abbreviation comes behind the competition word

parts.note: a cup is a competition with a trophy
PA is per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: After an annual match, tea with jam and bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the song line for Tea; a cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is British informal speech for a cup of tea, which the song pairs with jam and bread.

clue.text: From within deer, a female deer

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, across the word break

explanation.surface: Out of the deer family comes the female, as the song's line for Doe has it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the song's line for Doe; 'within' looks like the hiding signal but is itself part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hind is the female of the red deer, so it is a female deer.

clue.text: In some cases I'm pleading innocent

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A defendant claims innocence in some trials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; 'some' marks the letters spanning 'cases I'm pleading'.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple can mean guileless or naive, the sense of being innocent.

clue.text: Run racket in parts of Asia, or part of Italy

indicators.note: in places the run and the racket within the other letters
parts of says the word is broken up and its letters reassembled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
din means a racket or loud noise

explanation.surface: A noisy racket spreads through parts of Asia or part of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of' breaks the continent up; the run and the noise then sit inside the rearranged letters. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardinia is a large Mediterranean island that forms one of the regions of Italy.

clue.text: Nit-picking editor opposed to cutting inoffensive use of language

indicators.note: cutting says the editor and the opposed word slice into the abbreviation

parts.note: PC is political correctness, language avoiding offence
anti means opposed or against

explanation.surface: A fussy editor objects to politically correct language.
explanation.walkthrough: PC, short for politically correct, is language chosen to avoid giving offence; the two pieces split its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantic means overly concerned with minor details and rules, which is nit-picking.

clue.text: Old man guarding a venerated object in temple

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding, so the father word encloses the rest

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, an old man
a god is an idol or object of worship

explanation.surface: A father protecting a sacred idol in a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple in East Asia.
